content:
The [Retirement Calculator](/retirement-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Estimate your retirement nest egg and yearly income. Enter your current age, retirement age, current savings, monthly contribution and expected annual return and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

A retirement calculator estimates how much you'll have saved by retirement and how much annual income that could support, using the widely cited 4% withdrawal rule. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Finance tools include [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator), [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) and [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator).

## How to use the Retirement Calculator

Start by entering your current age, then entering your retirement age, entering your current savings, entering your monthly contribution and finally entering your expected annual return (%). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your current age.
2. Enter your retirement age.
3. Enter your current savings.
4. Enter your monthly contribution.
5. Enter your expected annual return (%).
6. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.

## Formula

Future value with monthly contributions; sustainable income ≈ 4% of the final balance per year.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Retirement Calculator](/retirement-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A 30-year-old with 25,000 saved who adds 500 a month at 6% could reach roughly 900,000 by 65 — about 36,000 a year at a 4% withdrawal rate. Try the same figures in the [Retirement Calculator](/retirement-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Current age: 30, Retirement age: 65, Current savings: 25000, Monthly contribution: 500, Expected annual return: 6 %), the [Retirement Calculator](/retirement-calculator) returns Nest egg at retirement: 915,443.94, Years to retirement: 35, Safe yearly income (4% rule): 36,617.76. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Capture any employer match — it's free money.
- Increase contributions each time you get a raise.
- Results are in today's money only if you use a real (after-inflation) return.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the 4% rule?

It suggests you can withdraw 4% of your portfolio in the first year of retirement, adjusted for inflation thereafter, with a low risk of running out over 30 years. Try it with your own numbers in the [Retirement Calculator](/retirement-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What return should I assume?

Many planners use 5–7% for a diversified portfolio, or 3–4% after inflation. Try it with your own numbers in the [Retirement Calculator](/retirement-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Retirement Calculator use?

Future value with monthly contributions; sustainable income ≈ 4% of the final balance per year. You can see it in action in the [Retirement Calculator](/retirement-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Retirement Calculator?

Just Current age, Retirement age, Current savings, Monthly contribution and Expected annual return. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
